correctness.rationale: Let m=2r. The m odd offsets are distinct when n≥2m. Summing the open-neighborhood equations gives m|C|=n, hence n is even. Subtracting equations at positions j and j+2 cancels m−1 terms and gives u_{i+2m}=u_i. If m divides n but 2m does not, translation by 2m and n also gives period m; each of the m/2 odd offsets modulo m occurs twice in each neighborhood sum, so a sum of 1 is impossible. If 2m divides n, all m odd offsets modulo 2m occur once, and the two parity equations require exactly one chosen class of each parity. This proves completeness, distinctness and the counts m² and n/m, including n=2m. Reduction modulo 2m maps the distinct neighbor offsets bijectively to the base's neighbor offsets, so the pullback statement holds.
residual_risks: The frozen script's finite checks were not executed. The proof, not those checks, classifies all permitted lifts.

evidence: The classified prime ratio n/|S| in Cameron–Yap–Zhou can equal 2 at the base; proper admissible lifts have even composite ratio. The coprimality assumptions of Cameron et al., Theorem 5.6, and Koohestani et al., Theorem 3.13, fail since |S| and n/|S| are even at every allowed order.
The cited prime-power existence results with exact valuation exclude the allowed orders when |S| is a power of 2 and otherwise do not apply to this even valency.

value.rationale: Once even order is forced by counting incidences, the connection set is exactly an interval in half-cycle coordinates. Tiling a cycle with equal translated runs forces each run to start immediately after the previous one; taking this choice twice gives every code, the period and the full count without further graph constraints. The frozen claim is a correct graph-language corollary, but does not add a structural phenomenon beyond that elementary interval classification or establish a motivated boundary involving genuinely different supports.
residual_risks: The value assessment is confined to the submitted consecutive odd-step family, not to total perfect codes on general circulants.
